title: Beasts of Aethelgard – Common Animals and the Pulse
content:
Pulse-Touched Beasts are ordinary animals altered by prolonged exposure to concentrated magic. A wolf living near a ley line intersection can grow to twice its normal size; its fur takes on an iridescent sheen, and its howl brings supernatural terror or calm, depending on the wolf's mood. Deer grazing in ancient groves sometimes grow antlers that glow faintly at night—attracting both mates and predators. Crows in the Sylvanweald speak words they overhear; they don't understand them, but they imitate them accurately, and travelers learn to monitor language in crow-infested areas. These creatures are fundamentally no different from their normal counterparts—they interbreed with normal members of their species, and the offspring are sometimes "touched" and sometimes not. They are treated with wary respect, because a bear touched by the Pulse is no more vicious than a normal bear, but is far more capable of acting on its malice.

Dire Beasts represent a more extreme aberration: creatures entirely evolved by magical pressures. Dire wolves roam the northern forests of Wintergard; their withers reach the chest height of a tall man, their fur so thick that arrows often fail to pierce them. They hunt with the tactical intelligence of an orc warband, and some experienced rangers claim they communicate through howling patterns that form a primitive language. Dire bears at the foot of the Ironvein Mountains can shatter dwarven defensive doors with a single blow; their pelts are prized for armor that repels blades as easily as natural leather repels rain. Wild boars, their tusks shrouded in a faint phosphorescent glow, charge through the ashes of the Wasteland with frenzied fury; hunting one is a rite of passage for young Federation warriors. These creatures are the apex predators in their territories, and while they can be defeated and killed, the wise keep their distance.
